title: Minimal romanized pronunciation for Tier-C phrases (M0 pull-forward)
context: PLAN v0.2 pulls minimal romanized pronunciation for Tier-C phrases forward from M1 to M0. The rationale: being understood under stress, including by low-literacy or non-Latin-script readers, is core to the responder↔newcomer value — not a backlog nicety. A responder who cannot read the target script needs a fallback to attempt spoken pronunciation of life-safety phrases (allergy, do-not-move, choking, bleeding). This is a narrow M0 scope: only Tier-C phrases, only a minimal romanization (not IPA audio), authored with the first translated pack and reviewed by a qualified speaker. Full pronunciation/transliteration support for all tiers is the separate M1 task (pronun-001). Note that romanization of medical-critical phrases is safety-sensitive: preserved tokens (numbers, emergency number, drug names) must remain exact, and the romanization is reviewed alongside the translation. The agent drafts; a qualified native/near-native speaker verifies; output is a draft unless sign-off is recorded.
objective: Add minimal romanized pronunciation fields for all Tier-C phrases in the first translated pack, authored alongside the translation and reviewed by a qualified speaker of the target language.
acceptanceCriteria: Every Tier-C phrase in the first translated pack gains a romanizedPronunciation field in phrases.yaml using a documented scheme (a widely-used romanization system for the language, or IPA-lite if no standard system exists; scheme stated per language)
Preserved tokens (numbers, units, emergency number) are romanized exactly as they appear in the translation, with no substitution or approximation
Romanization reviewed and signed off by a qualified native/near-native speaker of the target language, independent of drafting; sign-off recorded in review.yaml
Any UNCERTAIN: flags on romanization captured in agentFlags; no sign-off while flags are unresolved
Validates against the pack/phrase schema (romanizedPronunciation field added to schema); passes CI structural checks
Authored with the first translated pack (translate-001), not deferred to M1; M1 pronun-001 extends to all tiers
